options: A window with no fixed boundary at all
Variable-size windows that close after a gap of inactivity
Fixed-size and non-overlapping — every event belongs to exactly one window, and windows tile back-to-back with no gaps

questions.q: Why is a tumbling window the cheapest window shape to compute?
options: It skips storing any data
Each event is touched by exactly one window, and no window needs to be recomputed once it closes
It only works on batch-ingested data, which is always cheaper
It requires no aggregation logic at all
questions.explain: No overlap means no event is ever double-counted or reprocessed across windows.

questions.q: Why can't a tumbling window show a dashboard counter that updates smoothly every minute instead of jumping every 5?
